# app/controllers/api/v1/imports_controller.rb
require 'nokogiri'

module Api
  module V1
    class ImportsController < ApplicationController
      skip_before_action :verify_authenticity_token
      before_action :authenticate_api_key

      # POST /api/v1/imports/bulk
      # Accepts XML payload for bulk data import
      def bulk
        raw_body = request.body.read
        
        begin
          # Parse the XML document for processing
          doc = Nokogiri::XML(raw_body) do |config|
            config.nonet
          end
          
          # Validate root element
          unless doc.root&.name == 'import'
            return render json: { error: 'Invalid root element' }, status: :unprocessable_entity
          end

          records = []
          doc.xpath('//record').each do |record_node|
            record_data = {}
            record_node.children.each do |child|
              next if child.text? && child.content.strip.empty?
              record_data[child.name] = child.content
            end
            records << record_data
          end

          # Process records in background
          ImportWorker.perform_async(records)
          
          render json: { 
            status: 'accepted', 
            count: records.length,
            job_id: SecureRandom.uuid 
          }, status: :accepted

        rescue Nokogiri::XML::SyntaxError => e
          render json: { error: "XML parse error: #{e.message}" }, status: :bad_request
        rescue => e
          Rails.logger.error("Import failed: #{e.message}")
          render json: { error: 'Internal processing error' }, status: :internal_server_error
        end
      end

      # POST /api/v1/imports/validate
      # Validates XML structure without importing
      def validate
        raw_body = request.body.read
        
        doc = Nokogiri::XML(raw_body) do |config|
          config.nonet
        end
        
        errors = []
        doc.errors.each { |e| errors << e.message }
        
        if errors.any?
          render json: { valid: false, errors: errors }, status: :ok
        else
          record_count = doc.xpath('//record').length
          render json: { valid: true, record_count: record_count }, status: :ok
        end
      end

      private

      def authenticate_api_key
        api_key = request.headers['X-API-Key']
        unless api_key.present? && ApiKey.active.exists?(key: api_key)
          render json: { error: 'Unauthorized' }, status: :unauthorized
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

environment.description: Same Rails application on EKS 1.28 cluster. Namespace has label `pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: restricted` (Pod Security Standards in enforce mode). The restricted profile rejects pods with: runAsNonRoot not set to true, allowPrivilegeEscalation not false, seccompProfile not RuntimeDefault/Localhost, and critically any volume type other than configMap/emptyDir/projected/secret/downwardAPI/persistentVolumeClaim/CSI (hostPath is blocked). Additionally, the container image is built with a distroless base (gcr.io/distroless/ruby27-debian11) which strips /etc/passwd to a minimal entry, removes all SUID binaries, and the filesystem is read-only (readOnlyRootFilesystem: true in the pod spec). The container runs as UID 65534 (nobody). A Kyverno ClusterPolicy `restrict-volume-types` with `validationFailureAction: Enforce` independently blocks hostPath and hostPID. The combination means: no sensitive host files are accessible in the container filesystem, the service account token is projected as a bound token with 1h expiry and audience-restricted to the API server only, and /proc is mounted with hidepid=2.
